title: bundle-analysis
description: Learn about bundle-analysis. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Bundle analysis involves examining the composition, size, and dependencies of your JavaScript bundles. This helps identify large dependencies, duplicate code, and opportunities for optimization like code splitting and tree shaking.

Modern web applications can easily become multi-megabyte in size. Bundle analysis helps you understand what's in your bundles, identify optimization opportunities, and prevent performance regressions before they reach users.

data.title: Common Bundle Issues
data.code:
Common Bundle Issues Found Through Analysis:

1. Large Dependencies
   - Moment.js: 67KB (can use date-fns: 2KB)
   - Lodash: 70KB (can use lodash-es: 30KB)
   - Bootstrap: 150KB (can use CSS-only: 30KB)

2. Duplicate Code
   - Same library included multiple times
   - Polyfills included in multiple bundles
   - Utility functions duplicated across modules

3. Unused Code
   - Entire libraries imported but only 1 function used
   - Development code not removed from production
   - Dead code not eliminated by tree shaking

4. Poor Splitting
   - Everything in one giant bundle
   - Vendor code not separated from app code
   - No route-based code splitting

5. Large Assets
   - Unoptimized images
   - Unminified CSS/JS
   - Large font files not subsetted

data.text: webpack-bundle-analyzer creates an interactive treemap visualization of your webpack bundles, showing the size of each module and helping you identify large dependencies.

data.title: Webpack Bundle Analyzer Setup

data.text: Webpack's built-in performance hints warn when bundles exceed specified size limits. This provides immediate feedback during development.

data.title: Webpack Performance Hints

data.text: Source Map Explorer analyzes JavaScript bundles using source maps to show exactly which source files contribute to bundle size. This helps identify large files that need splitting.

data.title: Source Map Explorer Usage
data.content: Analyze bundle composition with source maps.
data.code:
# Install source-map-explorer
npm install --save-dev source-map-explorer

# Generate source maps in webpack config
development: {
  devtool: 'source-map'
}

# Analyze bundle
nsource-map-explorer dist/main.js

# Generate HTML report
source-map-explorer dist/main.js --html bundle-report.html

# Analyze multiple bundles
source-map-explorer dist/*.js --html combined-report.html

data.text: For projects using Rollup or Vite (which uses Rollup), use rollup-plugin-visualizer to analyze bundle composition and identify optimization opportunities.

data.title: Rollup Plugin Visualizer

data.text: Replace large dependencies with smaller alternatives that provide the same functionality.

data.title: Dependency Optimization
data.content: Replace heavy libraries with lighter alternatives.

data.text: Use bundle analysis to identify large modules that should be split into smaller, on-demand loaded chunks.

data.title: Identifying Splitting Opportunities
data.content: Use analysis to guide code splitting.
data.code:
Bundle Analysis Reveals:

Large Module: chart-library.js (300KB)
- Only used on dashboard page
- Contains 5 different chart types
- Users only view 1-2 charts per session

Action: Split by chart type
- chart-library-core.js (50KB) - shared code
- chart-library-line.js (60KB) - line charts
- chart-library-bar.js (60KB) - bar charts
- chart-library-pie.js (60KB) - pie charts
- chart-library-scatter.js (70KB) - scatter charts

Result:
- Dashboard load: 110KB (core + 2 chart types)
- Previous load: 300KB (all charts)
- Improvement: 63% reduction

data.title: Tree Shaking Analysis
data.content: Verify unused code is being removed.

data.text: Set up automated bundle analysis in your CI/CD pipeline to catch size regressions before deployment. Track bundle sizes over time to identify trends.

data.title: CI/CD Bundle Analysis
data.content: Automate bundle analysis in your pipeline.
data.code:
// .github/workflows/bundle-analysis.yml
name: Bundle Analysis
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  analyze:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v2
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npx webpack-bundle-analyzer dist/static/js/*.js --mode static --no-open
      - name: Upload bundle report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v2
        with:
          name: bundle-report
          path: bundle-report.html

// size-limit for automated checks
"size-limit": [
  {
    "path": "dist/*.js",
    "limit": "200 KB"
  },
  {
    "path": "dist/*.css",
    "limit": "50 KB"
  }
]

data.title: Bundle Size vs Network Size
data.text: Remember that bundle size (parsed) differs from network size (gzipped). Always analyze both. A 1MB bundle might be only 200KB gzipped, which changes optimization priorities.

terms.definition: The process of examining the composition, size, and dependencies of JavaScript bundles to identify optimization opportunities.
A webpack plugin that creates interactive treemap visualizations of bundle composition.
A tool that analyzes bundles using source maps to show which source files contribute to bundle size.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Bundle analysis reveals composition, size, and dependencies of your bundles
Use webpack-bundle-analyzer for interactive treemap visualization
Configure webpack performance hints for immediate size feedback
Source Map Explorer shows which source files contribute to bundle size
Identify large dependencies for replacement with lighter alternatives
Use analysis to guide code splitting decisions
Verify tree shaking is removing unused code effectively
Set up automated analysis in CI/CD to catch regressions
data.takeaway: Bundle analysis is essential for understanding and optimizing your application's JavaScript delivery, preventing performance regressions through data-driven optimization decisions.
